title: Joining the union and first professional job with Professor Longhair
summary: Encouraged by Mr. Houston, he joined the musicians' union around 1949-50 and began playing with Professor Longhair.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So, it seems like you would have gotten a lot of support for doing music, for playing

music. I had a lot of support from a lot of older musicians, like I tell you. I met a lot of them. A lot of them in that neighborhood where I lived and so forth. And by Mr. Houston coming to the house a lot of time when I'm in my junior year of high school, about 1949 to 50, is when he said, I give you permission to go in on and play. Well the union thing was just getting big then too. Union musicians couldn't play with the non-union musicians and all that kind of stuff. But if you join the union, it didn't cost you but eight dollars. Eight dollars in those days was like a lot of money. When did you join the union? It was about 1949 or 50. I joined the union, Sidney Cates. Sidney Cates was the Secretary of Treasury and so forth. And anyhow. Cuttrell was on the board. Oh yeah. Yeah. Well, Cuttrell wasn't on the board yet or not. He was just. He later came. Later came. Yeah. Where he took over for Mr. Houston. Yeah. Houston, Cates, right. Cuttrell and all those guys. Yeah. And 1496. That's right. So I joined a union through my first professional band to play with. Which one? Oh, Professor Longhair. Oh. Oh, okay. That's right. So that was my first professional band. Oh, okay. And we played at the hi-hat. Oh. As a matter of fact, the earlier days of the Johnson publication shows me playing with the hi-hat with Professor Longhair is in the sepia magazine of 1950.
